analysis:
Documentation-only PR (docs/architecture/inference.md, docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md). No code or threat-model YAML in this batch. The security-relevant claims are:

1. prefix-cache.md (~lines 65-70 and ~155-167) adds two exact 9B Bonsai identities (prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-9B-mlx-2bit and EigenLabs/Ternary-Bonsai-2-9B-MLX-2bit) to the exact-ID list of models that prefer paged attention. A new 'Bonsai complete state' paragraph says the 9B identities default to paged attention and the encrypted SSD prefix cache. This fits T-041, which already says SSD is default-on for every eligible CBv2 model with per-donation gating, HMAC lookup names, a 30-minute TTL and coordinator-authored cacheSalt. The docs state that authenticated cache identity, key availability, opt-outs, the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch and write-budget checks still apply. They add no new at-rest artifact kind and no TTL change. SEC-035 stays the accepted risk. Vision submissions are documented as cache-ineligible.

2. inference.md (~lines 622-655, 1164-1187) documents the 9B artifact sampling defaults and an explicit-only local MTP sidecar. The sidecar needs mtp_mode=on and mtp_drafter_path; auto does not download it. SpecDecArtifactFunnel keeps its identity, type and kill-switch gates. The weights are pinned to HF revision hashes. Public availability is explicitly not treated as qualification. This is relevant to T-012 and T-027 only as a reminder that weight integrity is still not cryptographically enforced.

3. Other inference.md text (the MiMo, MTP and Qwen4 sections) is descriptive and adds no new trust boundary. The changed 'fleet/private-candidate' wording was only narrowed to 'fleet/candidate'.

Coverage limit: the Swift code behind these claims was not supplied. A later pass should confirm that the 9B exact-ID cache default honours the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch and the per-donation gate, with cacheSalt scoping unchanged. It should also confirm that the 9B identity does not bypass the vision cache exclusion.
